configuration.thresholds_status: PROVISIONAL — linearly mapped from MiniLM; the LLM-judge silver study fits strict `covered` at ~0.80. Awaiting human gold (remaining #1) -> calibration (#2). Every covered/borderline/gap count and every heatmap cell colour moves if the bar moves.

modelled_results._note: Simulated by greedy facility-location: 'adding' a skill inserts a synthetic CLO that embeds the skill itself. An upper bound, not a forecast. Never report as an achieved result.

evaluation_ref._note: Precision/recall/F1 are properties of the INSTRUMENT (the 150-pair annotation study), not of a cohort run. Do not fill per-run.
evaluation_ref.gold_status: silver only (LLM judges, Cohen k=0.83); human gold 0/150

known_limits: KL is a point estimate with no confidence interval (remaining #6).
KL is encoder-bound: the curriculum profile is raw unthresholded max-cosine and BGE's floor for unrelated pairs is ~0.5, so KL is systematically damped.

KL is computed over the full ~571-skill segment, not just top_n. At the coverage magnitudes a single cohort can reach (~12-17/30), KL sits within ~6% of the 'teaches nothing' baseline (measured: null=0.3988, cohorts 0.374-0.378) and does not usefully separate cohorts. demand_weighted_coverage_percent is the primary cross-cohort metric; KL is a secondary distributional stat, not a ranking metric.
KL is not comparable across corpora of different size; only cross-cohort comparisons on the same market segment are valid.
Coverage is max cosine, not a percentage. coverage_rate_percent is the SHARE OF SKILLS covered (e.g. 12/30), never a cosine as a percent.

demand_weighted_coverage_percent = share of top_n's job-count mass that is covered (Sigma jobs[covered] / Sigma jobs[top_n]), i.e. how much of what employers ask for (within the top_n) is taught, not how many of top_n skills are ticked. Inherits the covered_at threshold (0.73, provisional; silver LLM-judge study suggests the true 'fully covered' bar is closer to 0.80) -- report the half-credit variant alongside it as a sensitivity bound.
